To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hypertensive patients showing high interpersonal and intraspersonal conflict develop more marked stress-induced blood pressure elevation than those showing low interpersonal and intrasperson conflict.
hypertensive patients with high anxiety and high conflict develop a greater blood pressure elevation under stressful conditions than those with low anxiety and low conflict.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the psychological and psychophysiological factors in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
the study of psychological and psychophysiological factors of the development of arterial hypertension.
the development of a psychosocial model of essential hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the psychological characteristics of hypertensive patients are not uniform and are determined by the severity of disease, its duration, and the degree of psychosocial stress to which the patients are exposed.
the psychological profile of essentially-hypetensive patients is more complex than that of coronary patients.
the psychological and psychophysiological profile of the hypertensive patient is not uniform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hypertensive patients who are most at risk of cardiovascular complications are those with a high level of anxiety and high interpersonal conflicts.
the psychophysiological characteristics and the psychological status of hypertensive patients are closely associated with the clinical course of the disease.

the hypertensive patients with the most severe disease and the highest blood pressure have a greater tendency to develop stress-induced blood pressure elevation and are more likely to have high anxiety and high conflict.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship of psychosocial stress to hypertension is not simple.
there are different patterns of physiological response of hypertensive and coronary heart disease patients to psychoemotional and psychosocial stress.
the psychosocial status should be considered when treating hypertension patients.
